answer: An AI-agent economy curbs Sybil attacks by mapping interaction graphs onto a peer-to-peer trust atlas. Nodes stake bilateral credit lines within a localized consensus reef, gating access through min-cut network capacity. To register influence, an adversary must prove an independent capital delta across disjoint paths, imposing real liquidity costs per identity. However, this path-dependent gating heavily penalizes newly deployed, honest agents that lack historical peer connections.
